source: PermaLoad ActorData + monster actor prefabs + ability prefabs + actor_scaler.json (UnityPy)
schema: monster_damage.json: average damage of ordinary monsters as a planner preset 'average monster of an area level 100 monolith' (extract_monster_damage.py). Monster selection: every ActorData with actorType Normal, spawnsInMonolith=1, not champion/omen/nemesis/harbinger/lone boss, name without test/dummy and with an actor prefab (the MonolithTimeline assets hold no per-monster list; ActorData.spawnsInMonolith is the flag used; monolithInZoneWeighting is stored per sample as weight but NOT used in the averages). Abilities = ability refs found in the monster's actor prefab (incl. CastSpeedManager overrides) plus sub-abilities (closure, depth 6); abilities of spawned helper actors are skipped. Per damage component: base100[i] = damage[i] * (1 + damageModifier) * product over the monster's own ActorStats Damage MORE stats (property 0, specialTag 0) whose tag mask is a subset of (component damageTags | ability tags | Hit or DoT | damage-type bit i; Elemental matches Fire/Cold/Lightning) * originalDamageApproximation[100] / originalDamageApproximation[L0] (L0 = ActorData.level, actor_scaler.json). NOT applied (the client does it): the ActorScaler (damageModifier[L]+1)*1.06-1 factor, corruption, rarity mods. Order of damage[7]: Physical, Fire, Cold, Lightning, Necrotic, Void, Poison. Categories: dot (isHit 0; values are PER SECOND = damage / timing.damageInterval, components without an interval are skipped), spell (hit, ability or component tags contain Spell), melee (hit, Melee and not Spell), ranged (hit, Bow or Throwing tag, or 'projectile' in the component/ability name and not Spell/Melee), other (kept for stats only). categories[cat]: samples, monsters, perType[type] = {n, mean, median, trimmedMean10 (10% cut each side), share} over samples that have that type (share = sum of that type / sum of totals of the category), total = same statistics of the per-hit (per-second for dot) total, critChanceMean / critMultiplierMean (plain means over samples). samples[] kept for audit.
